video.title: The Pros Grip Differently From You (with lesson examples)

classification.reason: The coach provides specific drills and cues, such as hitting with only two fingers to force the racket pivot at the top of the hand and nestling the top haptic reference before wrapping the fingers.

problem.title_as_question: Why do pros grip and pivot the racket differently from amateur players?
problem.definition: Many amateur players pivot the racket around the butt cap at the bottom of their hand instead of pivoting around the top of the hand (palm or V), losing effortless lag, control, and hitting slot perception.
problem.target_player: players who pivot off the bottom fingers, push the ball, or struggle to perceive racket momentum and lag

quotes.text: One of the things I check for every player is whether their racket is pivoting here as they swing or whether it's pivoting at the butt cap here
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: because so much of this lag elusive lag action that players are chasing comes from pivoting it at the top of your hand. And if you pivot the racket at the bottom of your hand, you will never uncover that
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: with the butt cap pivot at the bottom, the backswing the racket goes back and the forward swing it goes forward. But with the pivot at the top of the V, the V of your hand... now when I swing
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: all of these players are going to go from this more kind of pushing style to a real hit with the racket head and they're going to develop velocity control and spin all at the same time.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Now, our first and and most powerful tool for this is to take the bottom fingers off of the racket.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: players who pivot off the bottom a lot of times have these top references, these top haptic references disengage. Maybe they have gaps here or even if the hand is all the way around they just don't really know
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So, what we do is by forcing you to play with only two fingers, I am removing all of your haptic information down here and now I am forcing you to pivot here because you can't prevent it from pivoting
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And if your if your racket-hand interface isn't properly mapped, you can't perceive what's happening.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: if the part of your brain that communicates back to your the part of your nervous system that communicates back to your brain what you're doing with your racket isn't mapped onto the racket, then you'll never be able
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: neurologically, I have a sense of how I want the racket to hit the ball, how I want it to roll through the ball, and then that has to map onto a haptic sensation through the hand.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Start with this. This is the most important for control, for perceiving momentum, and then as we put our hand back on... we're trying to innervate either the bottom of the palm here or the front two fingers
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: when I use my bottom fingers, I can cheat the momentum of my racket head. So, even if my racket head wanted to hit the ball into the ground... I can cheat it and like wrist it up
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: with only two fingers, I can't cheat anymore. So, I have to perceive the racket's momentum, perceive how the racket head wants to move and then use my proximal links... to kind of be the powers humble guide
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: the wrist needs to be relaxed enough to bend backwards. Because if I have tension here, now I go here, and now the racket doesn't keep its momentum, and I swing forward, and I don't get anything.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: However, another great cue is just a feel for the same haptic signal that you got with the two finger... just the desire to feel that same sent signal through the hand will also cue you into relaxing
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If I like squeeze these bottom two fingers to like keep pushing the racket forward, I can really mess up the swing... Now, I'm like actively hitting with slow twitch flexion of the wrist.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Tension here should be passive. You should go here, feel the momentum through the swing, and then as you start to accelerate, you're going to feel your fingers squeeze because they are preventing... the handle from slipping out.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So, when we say relax, what we really mean is relax in this and then allow the tension to build. Don't don't try to make the tension build.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: watch Federer, watch Cilic, watch Alcaraz, they will go like this before many many of their forehands... watch Sam Querrey before every forehand he goes here and then he wraps his hands around.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: the very first step of any forehand is to innervate the top haptic reference, which is why you see Sinner, Alcaraz, Federer often starting here and then wrapping their fingers around
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Velocity is created proximally. Proximal meaning close to the spine. If you try to get velocity by by by hitting harder from here, that is going to break your signaling and it can even get you hurt.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: if you are struggling with velocity, often your brain will move your reference down the handle for more leverage. So, if I'm swinging like this, but I have no great sense of my scap, my
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We map the handle, we find a grip where he can actually perceive the hitting action, and that is the starting point for everything that we do on the stroke.
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: The racket pivots around the butt cap at the bottom of the hand rather than around the top of the hand.
The swing degenerates into a pushing action with mediocre ball velocity, spin, and depth control.
Player cannot feel the effortless lag, hitting slot, or racket momentum feedback during the swing.

causes.statement: Top haptic references at the palm or V are disengaged or loose, leading the player to fling the racket off the bottom fingers.
The hand-racket neural interface is not mapped in the nervous system, leaving the player blind to how the racket behaves in space.
Players use their bottom fingers to manipulate and cheat the racket trajectory instead of acting as a humble guide with proximal body rotation.
Excessive wrist stiffness or premature active squeezing of the bottom fingers interrupts elastic lag and momentum transfer.
When struggling for velocity, the brain intuitively shifts the pivot point down the handle for leverage rather than generating speed proximally.

angles.summary: Pivoting at the top of the hand causes the butt cap to move forward and outward when the tip moves back, creating an equal and opposite flip effect.
The hand and proximal body links act as the racket momentum's humble guide rather than an active forcing tool.
Pros like Federer, Sinner, and Alcaraz touch the racket into the top haptic reference before wrapping the bottom fingers around the handle.
Relaxation does not mean staying limp; it means staying relaxed during loading and allowing grip tension to build passively to keep from dropping the racket.

solutions.summary: Hit short forehands holding the racket with only the top two fingers to eliminate bottom leverage and force the pivot to occur at the top of the hand.
solutions.external_goal: racket momentum pivoting at the palm or V

solutions.summary: Progress from two fingers back to a full grip by sequentially innervating the bottom of the palm or front fingers to feel contact across the entire hand.
solutions.external_goal: innervating full contact between hand and handle

solutions.summary: Check that the wrist relaxes back by feeling for the exact same top-finger haptic pressure signal experienced during the two-finger drill.
solutions.external_goal: matching the two-finger haptic signal at the top of the hand

solutions.summary: Cue yourself to stay relaxed during the backswing and passively allow grip tension to build naturally as acceleration increases.
Start every shot preparation by nestling the top haptic reference (palm or V) into the handle first, and only then wrap the remaining fingers around.
solutions.external_goal: nestle the racket into the top haptic reference before wrapping fingers
